messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Increased inference 5xx and token latency in az1a (host egress jitter + DNS resolver errors). Automated health checks tripped at 16:02 UTC.

maria: seeing the same on console — p95 token latency up ~450ms and error rate ~4%. Marking pager. @ashok you're on rotation?

ashok: on it, grabbing metrics. any customer reports yet?

jules: internal telemetry shows a spike in connection resets from several inference nodes in az1a starting ~15:58 UTC. resolver lookup latencies also jump around same time.

maria: hypothesis: egress path jitter -> resolver timeouts -> some NLB connections stall and stream gRPC sessions back up with 502s. Could be host NIC scheduling jam or upstream resolver overload.

ashok: running quick checks: 
```
# tcpdump snippet from proxy host
15:59:02.123 IP hostX > resolver: DNS Standard query A example.com
15:59:02.872 IP resolver > hostX: DNS response (truncated)
# repeated truncation and retries
```

lia (cust-ops): two Dedicated customers on az1a reported elevated error rates to support. Notified them we are investigating.

maria: mitigation plan: 1) divert new requests away from az1a for eligible hosted models 2) drain problematic node pool in az1a 3) temporarily reduce connection keepalive on proxy to force reconnects to healthy backends.

ashok: applying route policy now — will steer traffic for non-Dedicated to eu-west-1 and usw2a where capacity exists. Executing Redwood Console route override: 
```
POST /v1/policy/route/override {
  "selector": "region:az1a AND tier:hosted",
  "action": "failover",
  "targets": ["eu-west-1","us-west-2"],
  "weight": [80,20]
}
```

maria: good. jules, please start drain on the node group with highest reset counts, scale up warm pool in other AZs. use drain with --ignore-daemonsets and set grace 30s.

jules: running: `kubectl drain node/inf-az1a-037 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

ashok: lowered NLB deregistration delay to 10s for the inference target group to speed failover. `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=10`

maria: also toggled short-term TTL for our internal resolver cache to avoid stampede — setting internal resolver TTL to 5s for critical service names.

lia (cust-ops): flagged both Dedicated customers with ETA ~25m for partial mitigation (traffic steering). Offering to escalate to SLA team if errors persist.

incident-bot: NOTE: Automation detected a 30% reduction in request volume to az1a after route override. Error rate reducing to 1.6% over last 2m.

jules: after drain some nodes re-registered fine in other AZs. Observed a few model-serving instances restarting due to prolonged gRPC stalls; restarted healthcheck watcher on those.

maria: running targeted probe across AZs to validate token latency and correctness: 
```
for region in eu-west-1 us-west-2 az1a; do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"ping"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' -o /tmp/out-$region && jq '.latency' /tmp/out-$region; done
```

ashok: results: eu-west-1 p95 110ms, us-west-2 p95 130ms, az1a p95 420ms. Good — steering helping.

lia (cust-ops): Customer A confirmed decreased errors; Customer B still seeing intermittent failures for dedicated capacity pinned to az1a. They cannot be moved automatically (reserved). Need ops to coordinate manual failover or offer temporary capacity swap.

maria: For dedicated tenants pinned to az1a we can: 1) provision temporary spare capacity in another AZ and migrate their model assignments, or 2) bail to a smaller compatible model in az1a as fallback. Which do we prefer?

ashok: prefer cross-AZ migrate for SLA customers. I'll open a migration window and coordinate with infra to tag and move model endpoints. Steps: snapshoting KV cache, update routing, warm instances in target AZ, then switch. ETA ~45m.

jules: infra note — egress jitter looks correlated with a subset of hosts on a single placement group; EC2 host-level telemetry shows TX queue delays and increased RX drop counters. I've raised a support case with AWS (case 1234567890) for host egress path degradation.

incident-bot: ACTION: on-call handoff scheduled. maria to hand off to ashok at 16:25 UTC.

maria: handing off — ashok taking lead, I'll stay on the thread for context. Key actions outstanding: keep steering active, complete Dedicated migration for Customer B, confirm AWS case progress, monitor error rate to <1%.

ashok: taking over. continuing migration prep and will post updates here. cc @lia (cust-ops) will send customer comms template now.

lia (cust-ops): sending customers an interim note: "We are experiencing elevated errors from a single AZ. We have routed most traffic away and are performing migrations for reserved workloads. Expect partial mitigation within ~45 minutes. We will update you once the dedicated endpoint is migrated or if we need to schedule a brief maintenance window."

maria: thanks team. keeping this thread open — will escalate to SEV if error rate climbs or migration blocks.

incident-bot: UPDATE: Error rate in az1a 0.9% (10m rolling), overall platform p95 now 160ms. Monitoring continues.
